lines.text: Step one: pick your list. On the Your list card, press Change.
A panel opens with the box Scan these stocks.
You can type in the box to search.
Lists come in groups: Index stocks, Sectors, F and O, My watchlists, and Type my own symbols. Each shows its size in brackets.
Index stocks holds the members of an index, such as NIFTY 50 or NIFTY 500. Sectors holds lists such as Banking or IT.
Pick a list. Here, a list of five hundred stocks.
To type your own, pick Type my own symbols, and type the symbols separated by commas or new lines.
A list can hold up to five hundred stocks, and Run scans the whole list. There is no fixed batch of fifty.
Press Done.
If a list cannot be loaded, an amber note says so, and the scan runs on NIFTY 50.
The card now shows the list's name and its number of stocks.
During a run, a line shows how far it is, for example 120 / 500 done. If your broker's limit slows it down, the line says so.
When it ends, the results header shows how many matched.
Information and education only, not investment advice.
Step two: pick the chart. On the Chart card, press Change.
Pick one of nine timeframes: 1, 3, 5, 15 or 30 minutes, 1 hour, Daily, Weekly or Monthly.
Daily, Weekly and Monthly work with or without a broker. 1 minute to 1 hour need your own connected broker.
Weekly and Monthly candles are built from daily candles.
Scans read closed candles only. A closed candle is final. The forming candle can still change, so a scan does not use it.
Only an alert can be set to read the forming candle, and the app marks that choice: earlier, but it can change before the close.
Press Done.
The Chart card shows the timeframe in words. A good place to start: Daily.
Inside a condition you can also read a candle further back, or one side on another timeframe. Episode three shows how.
Information and education only, not investment advice.
